Do you thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment where you can influence strategy, solve complex challenges, and build strong partnerships? Guardian is seeking an Enrollment Practice Leader to lead the end-to-end enrollment experience for our sales partners, brokers, employers, and members. In this role, you will serve as a trusted enrollment expert responsible for managing complex, high-impact cases, driving enrollment success, and delivering exceptional service experiences. You will partner across Sales, Client Management, and Enrollment teams to execute strategic enrollment solutions while identifying opportunities to improve processes, increase engagement, and support the continued growth of Guardian's enrollment capabilities. You Are A strategic and client-focused enrollment professional who thrives at the intersection of operational execution, relationship management, and enrollment consulting. You are energized by managing complex enrollment initiatives and collaborating with internal partners, brokers, and employers to deliver outstanding enrollment experiences. You have the ability to assess unique client needs, influence decisions, and develop creative solutions that drive participation and successful outcomes. You excel in environments where balancing multiple priorities, managing stakeholder expectations, and solving complex challenges are critical to success. You are a trusted advisor who leverages deep enrollment expertise, industry knowledge, and strong communication skills to guide clients and internal teams through the enrollment process. Success in this role requires a relentless focus on client outcomes, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and helping employees make informed benefits decisions that best meet their needs and those of their families. You Have Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience. 5+ years of experience in group benefits enrollment, benefits administration, client management, or a related field. Proven success managing high-volume and high-impact enrollment activities with measurable results. Experience supporting enrollment strategies, including one-on-one enrollments, decision support tools, digital enrollment campaigns, and employee education programs. Strong understanding of group benefits products and enrollment best practices. Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and lead initiatives across multiple teams and business partners. Experience mentoring team members and sharing operational best practices. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify process improvements and implement effective solutions. Exceptional presentation, communication, and relationship-management skills. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting brokers, employer groups, and distribution partners within the employee benefits industry. Knowledge of enrollment technologies, decision support engines, and enrollment platforms. Experience leveraging enrollment data and performance metrics to improve engagement and outcomes. Experience working in a consultative, client-facing role supporting large or complex accounts. Demonstrated ability to drive operational innovation and process optimization initiatives. You Will Lead and manage the end-to-end group benefits enrollment process, ensuring accurate execution, operational efficiency, and exceptional client outcomes. Serve as the primary Guardian Enrollment contact for distribution partners, brokers, employers, and internal stakeholders throughout the enrollment lifecycle. Gather enrollment requirements, coordinate case-level activities, and execute enrollment deliverables to support successful enrollment events. Provide proactive communication, status updates, and issue resolution to stakeholders while managing ongoing enrollment-related inquiries. Manage complex and high-impact enrollment cases while achieving performance, service, and engagement objectives. Partner closely with Sales, Client Management, and internal operational teams to drive enrollment strategy execution and client success. Provide strategic recommendations and actionable feedback to leadership to improve enrollment processes, client experiences, and team effectiveness. Mentor and support team members through knowledge sharing, coaching, and professional development opportunities. Identify, recommend, and implement innovative and cost-effective solutions that improve operational efficiency and enrollment outcomes. Reporting Relationships As our Enrollment Practice Leader, you will report to our Enrollment Strategy Leader, who reports to our Head of Enrollment. Job Title: Head of Financial Planning Strategy & Execution
Job Description: ROLE PURPOSE As a member of the Client Solutions leadership team, this role sets and executes Guardian’s enterprise financial planning strategy across channels and client segments. The leader builds a protection-first, holistic planning model that integrates insurance, retirement, investments, and wealth management; converts advanced-market expertise into actionable solutions; and scales consistent delivery for advisors and clients. Key Accountabilities Enterprise Planning Strategy & Operating Model ·       Partner with the Head of Client Solutions to align strategy and then design, evolve, and execute a comprehensive protection first, holistic financial planning strategy and framework. ·       Define the planning function’s governance, workflows, technology platforms, service standards, decision rights, and process improvements to enable efficient, consistent, and scalable execution. ·       Clarify how each planning discipline is reflected within the enterprise framework and how solutions align to distinct client and advisor segments. ·       Monitor competitive dynamics, industry trends, regulatory developments, and evolving client needs to keep the offering differentiated and relevant. Planning Solutions, Experience & Digital Scale ·       Design scalable planning models and deliverables for clients and advisors, with tailored approaches for complex HNW and UHNW needs. ·       Lead the evolution and adoption of digital planning capabilities that improve planning quality, advisor productivity, client engagement, and scale. ·       Translate complex financial concepts and technical thought leadership into practical tools, frameworks, case designs, and client-friendly recommendations. ·       Evaluate and integrate third-party capabilities where they strengthen the planning proposition and client experience. Advanced Markets & Complex Planning ·       Lead the GWAM strategy and team across thought leadership, case consultation, case design, business development, and sales campaigns, in alignment with Client Solutions and Wealth Management objectives. ·       Advance sophisticated solutions for HNW and UHNW clients, including estate planning, tax-efficient structures, insurance strategies, and legacy planning. ·       Partner with advisors, product teams, and internal and external specialists to address complex client needs and integrate advanced planning into broader engagement models. ·       Identify opportunities to strengthen Guardian’s HNW and UHNW value proposition through innovative, competitive planning solutions. Advisor, Field & Client Activation ·       Establish planning best practices, advisor enablement programs, training, and coaching strategies in partnership with distribution, regional and field leaders, product teams, and CSWM leadership. ·       Foster a planning-first culture centered on client needs, protection, implementation, and long-term relationship building. ·       Collaborate with Park Avenue Wealth Management and field partners to drive consistent execution while addressing segment-specific and complex planning needs. ·       Partner with marketing and communications to ensure the protection-first, holistic planning approach is reflected clearly and consistently in internal and external content. Enterprise Alignment, Performance & Risk ·       Influence product development, distribution strategy, and executive decision-making through data-driven insights, client outcomes, market intelligence, and planning trends. ·       Lead cross-functional initiatives by aligning stakeholders, managing dependencies, and accelerating enterprise priorities across product, operations, technology, marketing, legal, compliance, and distribution. ·       In partnership with the appropriate analytics and business teams, define metrics and reporting for plan utilization, advisor adoption, planning quality, client outcomes, productivity, and revenue impact. ·       Establish accountability and performance-management disciplines that improve financial planning quality, consistency, adoption, client outcomes, and organizational effectiveness. ·       Partner with legal and compliance to ensure advanced planning strategies, solutions, and supporting practices align with regulatory requirements, risk standards, and firm policies. Team & Leadership ·       Build and lead a high-performing team of financial planning and advanced-market professionals ·       Set clear priorities, operating rhythms, and development expectations; allocate expertise against the highest-value enterprise, advisor, and client needs. ·       Model sound judgment, integrity, collaboration, and executive-level communication while influencing senior stakeholders across the enterprise. Qualifications & Experience ·       15+ years of experience in financial services, wealth management, financial planning, or a related field, including significant leadership responsibility. ·       Experience leading planning or advice strategy within an insurance, investment, or wealth management organization. ·       Demonstrated experience supporting complex HNW and UHNW client needs and building scalable models for multiple client and advisor segments. ·       Deep understanding of how life insurance, annuities, retirement, investments, and protection solutions work together in a holistic financial plan. ·       Knowledge of advanced planning concepts and the ability to translate complex technical information into actionable, client- and advisor-friendly solutions. ·       Experience using technology, digital capabilities, data, and performance measures to improve planning quality, adoption, productivity, and business outcomes. ·       Proven ability to lead teams and influence senior stakeholders across distribution, product, operations, technology, marketing, legal, and compliance. ·       Strong strategic thinking, business acumen, communication, judgment, integrity, and collaboration skills. ·       Commitment to Guardian’s purpose of helping clients protect what matters and achieve long-term financial security. Licenses & Credentials ·       FINRA Series 7, 66, 63/65 required and series 24 required to obtain within 90 days upon hire. Job Description: Is the opportunity to join a culture where “We Do the Right Thing,” and “We Courageously Shape Our Future Together” important to you? If so, Guardian is seeking a motivated individual to join our team as a Workforce Planning Consultant. This role will report to the Head of Workforce Management, Group Benefits and serve as a strategic workforce planning consultant, trusted advisor, and subject-matter expert. You will own and evolve workforce planning methodologies, lead complex scenario planning, and translate workforce data into executive-ready recommendations that influence staffing decisions. You will be a partner with business leaders, Finance, Human Resources, Operations, Technology, and other stakeholders to evaluate workforce risks, challenge assumptions, and develop practical workforce strategies aligned with financial, operational, customer, and colleague objectives. Working with significant autonomy, you will lead specialized initiatives, create customized solutions to complex workforce challenges, and strengthen workforce planning capability through mentorship and knowledge transfer. You will Own and evolve workforce planning methodologies, standards, assumptions, and governance to support consistent, transparent, and defensible workforce decisions. Lead complex workforce planning and scenario modeling efforts that evaluate demand, productivity, shrinkage, staffing, capacity, service, and operational risk. Develop executive-ready workforce recommendations that clearly communicate alternatives, trade-offs, risks, and a recommended course of action. Serve as a strategic advisor to senior business leaders by translating workforce insights into practical strategies aligned with business priorities and operating commitments. Challenge workforce assumptions and established approaches when business conditions, emerging risks, or opportunities require a different solution. Evaluate strategic staffing alternatives, including hiring, cross-training, vendor, channel, skill, productivity, and operating-model scenarios. Influence workforce investment and resource decisions through objective analysis, consultative partnership, and clear articulation of business impact. Identify emerging workforce risks and opportunities, recommend mitigation strategies, and provide decision support during periods of material business change or uncertainty. Partner with Finance and business stakeholders to connect workforce plans with budgets, forecasts, productivity commitments, headcount strategies, and long-range business plans. Lead complex or specialized workforce initiatives from problem definition through recommendation, stakeholder alignment, implementation support, and outcome review. Mentor workforce planning talent by providing technical guidance, sharing best practices, and strengthening consultative and analytical capabilities across the team. Communicate difficult concepts and recommendations to diverse audiences, adapting the message to build understanding, alignment, and action. You have Required Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in business, finance, mathematics, statistics, data science, analytics, or a related field, or comparable professional experience. 10+ years of experience in workforce management, workforce planning, capacity planning, workforce analytics, or a related discipline, with demonstrated ownership of complex planning work and business recommendations. Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to synthesize incomplete or conflicting information and develop customized solutions. Experience advising senior leaders, challenging assumptions constructively, explaining trade-offs, and influencing decisions without formal authority. Exceptional written, verbal, facilitation, and presentation skills, including the judgment and discretion required for sensitive workforce discussions. Proven ability to translate complex quantitative analysis into clear executive narratives, recommendations, and decisions. Experience leading complex or specialized projects across multiple stakeholders in a matrixed organization. A self-directed, collaborative, and improvement-oriented mindset, with the ability to manage competing priorities and operate effectively with guidance only in the most complex situations. Preferred Qualifications: Specialized expertise in workforce forecasting, staffing and capacity modeling, scenario planning, productivity analysis, shrinkage, service-level dynamics, and workforce risk assessment in both back office and contact center environments. Demonstrated ability to design, adapt, and govern workforce planning methodologies rather than only apply established models. Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect workforce decisions to service, cost, quality, customer, colleague, and operational outcomes. Expert proficiency with analytical and presentation tools such as Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with workforce management, data visualization, forecasting, or modeling platforms such as Verint, Tableau, or comparable tools. Experience mentoring analysts or serving as a technical advisor and thought leader within a workforce planning or analytics function. Experience working directly with financial advisors, firms, or territory-based sales teams. Follow up with broker/producer regarding status of renewals and add issue quotes while also engaging the Sales Rep, as needed, to help close the renewal or sale. Provide renewal rate relief for groups under 100 lives through negotiations with underwriting, as well as determining and generating plan alternative options Serve as subject matter expert on various Guardian systems, capabilities, products, and workflow procedures You have: Excellent written and oral communication skills Excellent customer service soft skills Very strong mathematical aptitude and analytical skills Strong consultative, negotiation, persuasion, and influencing skills with a sales orientation Ability to build and maintain collaborative working relationships at all levels A client-focused approach Personal accountability Strong planning and organizational skills with ability to multi-task Ability to easily adapt to change Ability to work independently and in a group setting Motivation to meet goals:  Meet persistency goals, renewal target goals, cross-sell goals (add issue), etc. Computer proficiency in Outlook, Skype, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Salesforce, GCRS, Siebel, CPS, Phoenix, Business Objects, etc. Ability to represent Guardian in a professional manner The successful hire must be based in Syracuse, NY or Albany, NY. The work arrangement will be remote. Knowledge: Solid knowledge of group insurance products, contracts, and services. Group insurance products include dental (PPO, DHMO, fully insured and ASO), vision, life, accident, short- and long-term disability (fully insured and ASO), statutory disability, supplemental health, voluntary benefits, and leave management (federal, state, and local). Solid knowledge of financing methodologies and strategies (fully insured and alternate funding) Solid knowledge of group insurance underwriting principles, methodologies, and practices Education: BA or BS Degree is preferred. Will consider work experience equivalent. Experience: 3 to 5 years of insurance industry experience, preferably in a sales environment Demonstrated success in servicing brokers/producers/customers Other: Eligible for variable compensation for persistency and renewal target bonus and cross-sell/add-issue bonus, according to the current year Group Sales Incentive Compensation Plan for Client Manager Associates Must achieve required industry licensing within 90 days of date of hire and maintain license through completing Continuing Education requirements Location and Work Arrangement: The successful candidate must be based in the assigned territory: Syracuse, NY or Albany, NY. Analytical: Ability to analyze operational, financial, workforce, and customer data to identify opportunities, quantify impact, and influence recommendations. We drive a high-performance culture across our Legal, Compliance, and Government Affairs functions, aligned to “what” we deliver (i.e., our goals and objectives) and “how” we demonstrate our values and behaviors while focusing on the customer. We do this through leveraging a series of core capabilities, which includes accountability, interpersonal effectiveness, ability to demonstrate business savvy, being a subject matter expert, all while supporting the Law Department’s Mission to be a trusted advocate and advisor to drive strategic solutions that advance Guardian’s purpose, priorities, and values. A successful candidate will have excellent research and organizational skills, and business judgment as you will be required to understand and manage the laws and regulations affecting individual insurance products and wealth management offerings and provide practical advice in a rapidly changing and high-profile regulatory environment. You will also need to draft applicable agreements with distribution partners and help to facilitate the succession of general agencies. The ability to influence and drive proactive partnership in a changing business environment is critical. You will develop cross-business connections, provide industry perspective and best practices guidance while considering long-term outcomes and the needs of partners/clients when providing advice. An effective communicator, with a proven record of influencing cross-functional teams establishing and leading strong relationships with critical partners and executive stakeholders. Able to effectively convey ideas and engage in meaningful conversations. You will Provide advice and counsel to CSWM strategies and innovation initiatives in their organizations. Participate in external forums, build partnerships internally across Guardian, and help ensure that Guardian’s CSWM business practices and policies are compliant with applicable law. Advise and assist with the implementation of new distribution and wealth management related laws and regulations. Represent the practice group as a key advisor to stakeholders to establish, inform, and maintain company-wide compliant policies. Provide effective, prompt compliance advice and support business compliance, rectifying problems, and responding to emerging challenges. Keep informed regarding pending industry changes, trends, and best practices and assess the potential impact of these changes on organizational processes. You have 7 – 10 years of experience, preferably in connection with the life insurance and/or wealth management industries. JD and licensed to practice law in New York Ability to address complex and challenging issues and communicate effectively with business leaders at all levels to optimize risk management, productivity, and communication. Ability to work in a dynamic, hands-on, fast-paced environment and respond to questions from business areas and a complex subsidiary organization. Lead remediation efforts related to operational issues, audit findings, compliance exceptions, escalations, and data integrity concerns across all plans. Coordinate and oversee nondiscrimination testing, regulatory filings, audits, annual limits, and other compliance requirements in partnership with service providers and internal partners. Support alignment among plan documents, Summary Plan Descriptions, administrative practices, and operational procedures across all retirement plans. Support vendor sourcing, transitions, implementations, and operating model changes, as needed. Monitor vendor performance against agreed-upon service standards and identify opportunities for continuous improvement. Support retirement-related operating model improvements, process transformations, and implementation of new services. Support automation, analytics, AI-enabled solutions, and process simplification initiatives to improve efficiency and strengthen controls. Support strategic retirement initiatives, vendor RFP and transitions, and long-term retirement program evolution aligned with organizational priorities. Able to lead projects that implement new services and programs, collaborate effectively with stakeholders, and contribute insights to leadership. An innovative thinker who continuously seeks opportunities to improve participant outcomes, strengthen controls, and simplify operations. Experience reviewing and implementing operating model improvements within a highly regulated environment. Experience supporting complex vendor relationships and influencing service provider performance. Proven ability to identify, assess, and manage operational, compliance, and fiduciary risk. Advanced analytical and Excel skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience in a large corporate or financial services environment. Job Title: Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability
Job Description: Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability Reports To Head of Technology Operations Department Enterprise Technology Position Summary The Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability is responsible for defining and executing the enterprise observability strategy, operating model, and platform roadmap that enable proactive, predictive, and resilient technology operations. This leader owns the enterprise capabilities for monitoring, telemetry, event intelligence, operational analytics, and observability engineering, ensuring technology services are observable, measurable, actionable, and continuously improving. The role serves as the operational intelligence leader across Enterprise Technology, providing the platforms, standards, insights, and governance required to improve service reliability, accelerate issue detection and resolution, and support modern operational practices. This leader partners closely with infrastructure, cloud, middleware, application, security, resiliency, and service management teams to build a unified enterprise-wide observability capability. Key Responsibilities Enterprise Observability Strategy Define and execute the enterprise observability vision, strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap. Establish standards and governance for monitoring, logging, metrics, tracing, telemetry, alerting, and service observability. Lead the evolution of observability capabilities from reactive monitoring toward proactive, predictive, and automated operations. Drive enterprise adoption of modern observability practices, frameworks, and engineering standards. Observability Platform Ownership Own the strategy, architecture, lifecycle, and operation of enterprise monitoring and observability platforms. Lead platform modernization, tool rationalization, capability expansion, and service offering improvements. Manage vendor relationships, contracts, platform investments, and cost optimization efforts. Ensure scalability, availability, resilience, and ongoing enhancement of observability tooling and services. Monitoring and Telemetry Services Establish enterprise monitoring and instrumentation standards across infrastructure, cloud, middleware, applications, databases, and digital services. Improve monitoring coverage, telemetry quality, alert effectiveness, signal quality, and operational visibility. Drive adoption of distributed tracing, service dependency mapping, and end-to-end transaction monitoring. Ensure service health and operational data are consistently available across the technology landscape. Operational Intelligence and AIOps Lead implementation of operational analytics, event intelligence, anomaly detection, predictive insights, and AIOps capabilities. Develop dashboards, scorecards, and reporting that provide actionable operational intelligence to technology leadership. Enable intelligent event correlation, noise reduction, automated diagnostics, and automated operational workflows. Partner with engineering and operations teams to use observability data for continuous improvement and outage prevention. Reliability and Incident Enablement Partner with technology teams to improve detection, response, recovery, and root cause analysis capabilities. Establish observability practices that improve service reliability, operational resilience, and customer experience. Drive post-incident learning and identification of automation opportunities. Provide enterprise visibility into technology health, performance trends, capacity risks, and reliability risks. Leadership and Talent Development Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of observability engineers, platform engineers, and operational intelligence specialists. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, operational excellence, continuous learning, and cross-functional partnership. Lead organizational adoption of observability best practices through enablement, coaching, and stakeholder engagement. Establish strong partnerships across technology, cybersecurity, architecture, engineering, operations, resiliency, and service management functions. Qualifications 10+ years of experience in infrastructure operations, platform engineering, observability, reliability engineering, or related technology disciplines. 5+ years of experience leading enterprise-scale engineering or operational teams. Deep expertise in observability platforms, monitoring technologies, telemetry pipelines, logging, metrics, distributed tracing, and operational analytics. Demonstrated experience implementing enterprise monitoring strategies and improving operational reliability at scale. Strong understanding of cloud platforms, hybrid infrastructure, automation, DevOps practices, and modern operational architectures. Experience leading organizational transformation and driving adoption of new operational capabilities. Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and strategic planning skills. Success Measures Increased enterprise monitoring and observability coverage. Reduced mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR). Improved signal quality and reduced alert fatigue. Increased adoption of observability standards and platform capabilities. Improved service reliability, operational resilience, and operational efficiency. Expansion of predictive analytics, automation, and AIOps capabilities across Enterprise Technology. Job Title: Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation
Job Description: The Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation is a senior leadership role responsible for the strategic evolution, differentiation, and commercial success of our open‑architecture wealth management product platform. This individual wakes up every day thinking about what’s next —how product, partners, packaging, and go‑to‑market strategy come together to create a compelling, modern, and advisor‑centric platform across fee‑based advisory, annuities, and alternatives. We do not manufacture products. Our competitive advantage comes from curation, partnership, design, positioning, and delivery . This role exists to ensure our platform is not merely comprehensive—but distinctive, relevant, and growth‑oriented . The role works horizontally across the organization —marketing, sales, business development, training, product management—and externally with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and portfolio managers . Success requires influence without direct ownership, entrepreneurial energy, and a strong commercial mindset. Key Responsibilities Product Strategy & Innovation Own the forward‑looking product strategy across advisory, annuities, and alternatives within an open‑architecture ecosystem. Identify gaps, white spaces, and emerging opportunities driven by advisor needs, client behavior, regulation, and competitive dynamics. Design differentiated product constructs, solutions, and portfolios by creatively leveraging third‑party partners rather than manufacturing products. Translate industry trends (e.g., retirement income, tax efficiency, private markets, managed solutions, model portfolios) into actionable platform initiatives. Platform Differentiation & Go‑to‑Market Develop clear go‑to‑market strategies for platform capabilities, including positioning, messaging, and advisor value propositions. Partner closely with Marketing to ensure product stories are simple, compelling, and commercially effective . Work with Sales and Business Development to align product strategy with advisor adoption, growth objectives, and field readiness . Drive clarity around why advisors should use specific solutions—not just what is available. Partner Strategy & Ecosystem Management Serve as a senior point of engagement with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and product sponsors . Evaluate, onboard, and rationalize partners with a focus on quality, differentiation, economics, and strategic fit . Co‑create solutions with partners where appropriate, including custom portfolios, white‑labeled offerings, or exclusive access strategies . Maintain a strong commercial lens on platform economics, scalability, and advisor impact. Cross‑Functional Leadership & Influence Act as a strategic connector across Product Management, Sales, Marketing, Training, and Business Development. Provide strategic direction while leveraging existing execution teams for implementation. Influence priorities and outcomes without direct people ownership , using clarity, credibility, and collaboration. Partner with Training and Sales Enablement to ensure advisors understand not just products—but how to use them in holistic planning conversations . What Success Looks Like Advisors view the platform as thoughtful, differentiated, and easy to position with clients . Product initiatives are clearly linked to advisor adoption, client outcomes, and revenue growth . Partners see the firm as a strategic collaborator , not just a distributor. The platform evolves proactively— not reactively —to market and advisor needs. Qualifications & Experience 10+ years of experience in wealth management, asset management, insurance, or fintech, with exposure to RIA and broker‑dealer environments . Deep knowledge of fee‑based advisory, annuities, alternatives, and managed solutions . Demonstrated ability to build or evolve open‑architecture platforms without manufacturing products. Strong commercial and go‑to‑market orientation —understands how strategy translates into advisor behavior. Proven success working cross‑functionally and influencing outcomes without direct authority. Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to balance vision with practical execution . Comfortable operating with ambiguity and turning ideas into scalable initiatives. Why This Role Matters This role ensures our product platform moves from “robust but pedestrian” to strategically curated, commercially sharp, and advisor‑obsessed —without disrupting what already works operationally. It complements strong execution with vision, innovation, and market leadership . Job Description: Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Understand and participate across portfolio initiatives, connect dependencies and opportunities across programs to optimize solutions, increase reuse, and reduce data waste. Drive the adoption of a data product operating model across the organization. Champion data product thinking by promoting customer-centric design, product ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable business value. Establish best practices for discoverability, usability, interoperability, governance, and consumption of enterprise data products. Translate business strategy into scalable technology, data, and analytics solutions. Lead discovery workshops and data solution design sessions across underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, reporting, and digital channels. Influence enterprise technology strategy by identifying reusable capabilities and modernization opportunities. Develop reusable frameworks, accelerators, and reference architectures to improve data delivery speed, consistency, and reuse. Design modern data platforms and pipelines that support real-time and batch processing, scalable data integration, and enterprise analytics needs. Ensure high-quality, trusted data through governance, observability, lineage, metadata, and automated data quality controls. Collaborate with data engineering, product, and AI teams to operationalize AI-enabled data solutions within the data ecosystem. Foster collaboration across architecture, engineering, product management, security, data, AI, and business teams. You Have (Required Qualifications) : Deep experience designing and governing enterprise-scale solution architectures across multiple teams and domains. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns. Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems, including application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows. Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level. Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed. Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority. Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction. Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs. This role will work closely with core FPRS/CSWM business value streams (e.g., distribution mgmt., shop, purchasing, service, claims, etc.) to define, shape, prioritize and lead the delivery and evolution of key data and information product (‘Products’) solutions supporting business objectives. More specifically, this role will drive the capture and planning for new demand of features and/or enhancements to Guardian’s data Products as articulated by key business leaders from one or more key value stream and/or the respective FPRS/CSWM FP&A functional BI leader. These data Products include everything from consumer-facing analytics (reports/dashboards), to inter/intra-application data services (APIs/extracts/shares), to data services supporting AI/GenAI automation, to the underlying data definitions and reference data that define the FPRS/CSWM businesses. This leader will embed best practices, enable accurate and consistent decision-making, and cultivate a culture of continuous improvement while proactively preparing the organization for operational, technological, and capability change. A central responsibility of this role is to ensure underwriting excellence is achieved and sustained through strong execution, readiness, and adoption. Develop and execute operational excellence strategies aligned to underwriting goals, enterprise priorities, and customer outcomes. Assess change impact and readiness across underwriting teams, translating operational initiatives into clear people, role, skill, and behavior implications. Partner with underwriting leaders to strengthen change leadership capability, ensuring leaders actively sponsor, reinforce, and role-model new ways of working. Identify adoption risks and cultural barriers early, implementing mitigation strategies that support sustained behavioral change. Ensure operational improvements are reinforced through updated operating rhythms, performance expectations, governance, and training—not just documented outcomes. Provide ongoing support, tools, and resources that enable colleagues to work more efficiently and confidently. Engage stakeholders at all levels to foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and urgent execution. Instill a strong linkage between operational excellence, consumer-centricity, and underwriting excellence. A people-oriented, change-capable leader who balances execution rigor with adoption and sustainability. Results-driven with a deep sense of accountability and ownership. Strong background in Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement methodologies. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate insight into action. Excellent leadership and stakeholder engagement skills, including influencing at senior levels. Proficiency in data analysis, reporting tools, and operational performance management. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
